 **UBS TMI: Weekend Wrap (9/21-9/25)

 

What a week. The market has spent the back-to-school season trying to process a truly exhausting menu of overhangs… from agentic AI fears, lingering “pacing the frontier” debate, Trump-Xi meetings, post-FOMC paralysis, ORCL/datacenter mayhem, and a consumer backdrop that nobody can quite decide is fine or slowly deteriorating. And while we can stare at the screens all day and debate what’s driving every tick, the clearest message from our flow is that just isn’t a ton of real direction or conviction underneath the surface. Post-Meta Connect, liquidity was fairly thin, with composite volumes well below the 1H of the week’s levels and not much meaningful regrossing to speak of. So here we are, caught between two potential regime shifts: macro and AI. Neither has given investors enough clarity to plant a flag, and until one does, this market probably remains less about “what do I fundamentally believe?” and more about positioning. Which leaves us with a familiar recipe: intraday whiplash, muted factor leadership, aggressive rotations, positioning resets, and short-covering rallies that can feel much more meaningful in the moment than they ultimately are.  For next week, the biggest question will be: can geopolitical de-escalation take some heat out of oil and yields? A sustained move lower in both would go a long way toward clearing the macro air, potentially pulling sidelined capital back into the market, broadening participation, and giving AI leadership another opportunity to reassert itself.

 

Per usual, see below for key incomings of the week, a preview of the week to come and the latest sentiment/positioning screens. Hope everyone has a great rest of the weekend! CD

 

KEY INCOMINGS

  • META MUSE: Feels like several years of META capex PTSD got washed away in a week. Muse Mania was in full force with META +13% this week, and while Friday finally introduced the stock to the concept of “down,” the remarkable part has been the near-total absence of pushback. Seriously, where are the nitpicks? All I heard was product feedback is great, monetization has barely started, and Muse is the first meaningful sign that Zuckerberg’s capex bonfire may have actually been an investment rather than performance art. That said, don’t mistake the price action for an LO religious conversion. We have NOT seen LOs driving flow this week. They’ve been happy to wait for sturdier ROI receipts, and while Muse certainly helps, whether this has real staying power or becomes the next OpenClaw craze is TBD. Think this all goes to show the AI FOMO trade in its prime as investor appear more than willing to look through the day-to-day noise because the fear of missing what META becomes is starting to outweigh any execution risks. OpenAI DevDay next week remains a risk, though I keep hearing skepticism that OpenAI can own consumer agents the way META potentially can, particularly given GPT’s compute constraints and the recent Astra stall. Which raises a fascinating endgame: META owns consumer AI/agents, while GPT owns enterprise?

 

  • CONSUMER FRICTION BASKET: In case you missed it, we officially launched our new Consumer Friction baskets this week in the US {UBXXCFRC} and Europe {UBXECFRC}, a timely addition to the toolkit amid ongoing Muse Mania and the broader agentic AI conversation. Building this basket we focused on the question what happens when AI makes it much easier for consumers to shop around and switch providers? From there, we identified six key sub-groups across Insurance, Telcos and Internet where those frictions are particularly prevalent. I’ve probably exhausted everyone’s inboxes with my thoughts on agentic risk already, particularly across Telco & Internet, so I’ll spare you another TED Talk. What I will say is that the name I received by far the MOST pushback on, specifically on whether it deserved to be in the basket at all, was… ABNB

 

  • CRWV INITIATION: Karl Keirstead makes his debut in his neocloud coverage, launching on CRWV with a BUY Rating and a $120 PT, as strong demand and revs/GW growth signals outweigh leverage/credit concerns and investor sentiment remains just cautious enough to make the risk-reward is favorable. So yes,  the easier call, in light of persistent leverage concerns, would be to launch with a more neutral/cautious stance and wait. But Karl believes the Street may be under-appreciating the strength and durability of AI compute demand (from enterprises, not just the frontier labs), GPU pricing trends (driving a ramp in revenue per GW from ~$11 billion today to $15+ billion over time), and the fact that (based on checks outlined in this report) CoreWeave has established a reputation for reliability and performance that distinguishes it from peers. A positive call on CoreWeave shares is a de facto call that investors will soon rotate back into the long-AI trade, a scenario that seems increasingly likely given the muted sentiment, strong demand signals and reported frontier lab growth. Link to note

 

  • BITCOIN MINING LAUNCH: Ryan Gravett initiated on five AI colocation names, HUT, WULF, APLD, CORZ & CIFR, all rated Buy, with 100+ pages of industry and company-specific work to supplement his recommendation. The key to the thesis is power. As AI data center demand has exploded, time to power has become one of the biggest constraints on new development. That puts these former crypto miners in a uniquely attractive position: their existing grid interconnects have already helped unlock nearly 5GW of leased colocation capacity, with another 12GW of potential expansion. So yes, there’s an element of right place, right time, but these companies also own the assets and have the capabilities needed to provide one of the scarcest inputs into the massive AI infrastructure buildout. There are risks, of course, but Ryan sees the recent pullback as creating an attractive entry point. Continued expansion of the AI frontier, growing open-source adoption and broader AI penetration could ultimately set these names up for outsized returns. Link to note

 

  • WHAT’S NEW IN THE AI DEBATE? Karl Keirstead and team revisit the latest AI debates and emerging trends, coming off recent conferences which kept them constructive on the (no-longer-consensus) long AI trade. In terms of what feels “new”, Karl flags 1) a much bigger focus on AI security, sandboxing and real-time agent observability, especially post the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident and the roll out of agents 2) a clear uptick in enterprise demand to fine-tune (mostly open) foundation models to build custom or private AI models 3) Nvidia, via Nemotron and OpenShell, has quickly become a real presence up the AI stack. 4) Token spend optimization has gone mainstream as AI bills have risen so quickly YTD but importantly, his checks suggest that AI spend is STILL ramping materially. Interestingly enough, he also notes that the “pacing the frontier” debate has settled down, open/custom models are gaining share (but the share going to frontier labs remains very high), and revenue per GW of AI data center capacity is moving higher.

 

WHAT’S ON TAP?

With that in mind, friendly reminder that Stephen and team keep a pretty robust spreadsheet tracking every tweak to each expert’s estimates, quarter by quarter for anyone looking to dig in. TMT TRADING FLOW:  An overall positive week for Tech with AI infrastructure continuing to act as a dominant driver, ultimately supporting Optical, Memory, and Compute. Equipment names also outperformed while large cap AI chip leaders lagged (NVDA, AVGO). Software more mixed, with notable dispersion between AI-driven winners and names facing company-specific headwinds. PLTR and MSFT led, while INTU, ORCL, and ADBE were notable laggards – highlighting data center execution and broader macro risk. Flow wise, early week saw buying across Optical, though profit taking across Memory and Compute more of a theme. As the week progressed, turned better to buy in Semis broadly (a shift from the selling into the strength early week) and covering across the apps names in Software. META MUSE dominated the discussion for most of the week with pockets within Media and Telcos clearly in the spotlight being put into the disruption bucket with OTAs, Cable and Media Subscription names deep in the red for the week. Wireless faired a bit better. Towers remained a source of funds with move higher in rates being cited as the main driver.  Broadcasters and Networks briefly ran on THE PSKY/WBD settlement but gave back most of the gains with LION under pressure Friday after a competitor initiation. Rideshare names also better for sale as investors continued to worry about a consumer slowdown but also the action in crude. Legacy entertainment names were mixed this week with FWONK & LYV outperforming TKO where we got a lot of questions. Looking at recent preference shifts. DIS > CMCSA. T > VZ & TMUS. PINS >SNAP. Payments overall higher heading into Friday with a new US/Iran peace deal coming into focus. The chatter on the deal ultimately triggering a grind back to positive territory after a week filled with swings in and out of the green. AI, blockchain, and macro related narratives all contributing to the moves alongside a flurry of single stock catalysts coming to the forefront – SOFI/MA stablecoin deal, XYZ business integration with AAPL/WDAY, and PYPL partnership with META. XYZ benefiting the most from their partnership on top of the positive macro backdrop late week – a clear winner yesterday vs the rest of Acquirers. Performance and action at the subsector level very similar with most spaces (Lenders, Acquirers, Networks) all ending the week flat to marginally higher or lower. Acquirers slightly > Lenders / Networks with most names better to buy into the declines seen earlier in the week.
